title: Stateful Orders Database
description:
**SITUATION:**

QuickByte needs a small database for order history. Unlike Order Processor (any healthy copy can take the next request), database copies are **not interchangeable**:

- each copy needs a **stable name** (so ops and peers always know which is which)
- each copy needs **its own disk** (so data does not get overwritten by a random replacement Pod)

A normal Deployment gives Pods throwaway names and is a poor fit. You need the Kubernetes workload type built for this shape.

This lab introduces a **StatefulSet** for orders-db: stable Pod names and per-replica disks. Treat this differently from Order Processor Deployments — database copies are not interchangeable.
[DevSetu Blog — StatefulSets](/play/devops-engineer/kubernetes/read/statefulsets)

**YOUR TASK:**

1. Create a **StatefulSet** named `orders-db` running Postgres with **2** copies.
2. Verify both copies are **Ready** and each got its **own** disk automatically.

**SPEC:**

- StatefulSet name: `orders-db`
- Replicas: `2`
- `spec.serviceName`: `orders-db` (name used for stable DNS — you wire the matching Service in the next challenge)
- Pod labels: `app=orders-db`, `tier=data`
- Pod `securityContext.fsGroup`: `70` (alpine postgres UID/GID — so the PVC is writable)
- Container name: `postgres`
- Image: `postgres:16-alpine`
- `containerPort`: `5432`
- Env:
  - `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`: `quickbyte-lab`
  - `POSTGRES_DB`: `orders`
  - `PGDATA`: `/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata` (subdir on the volume — do not use the volume root as PGDATA)
- Resource requests: `20m` CPU, `64Mi` memory
- Resource limits: `100m` CPU, `128Mi` memory
- Recommended: container args `-c shared_buffers=16MB` so Postgres shared memory fits the 128Mi limit
- `volumeClaimTemplates`:
  - name: `data`
  - accessModes: `["ReadWriteOnce"]`
  - storage: `500Mi`
  - `storageClassName`: `gp2` (cluster StorageClass for dynamic EBS)
- Mount `data` at `/var/lib/postgresql/data`
- Ready: **2/2** replicas Ready

**GOOD PRACTICES:**

- Manifest: `orders-db-sts-l20.yaml`.
- Use a **StatefulSet**, not a Deployment.
- Do **not** skip `serviceName: orders-db`.
- Work only in your lab namespace (not `default`).

hints: Your namespace is in the lab chrome and in $LEARNER_NS — kubectl already defaults there.
Set volumeClaimTemplates storageClassName to gp2 so PVCs can provision dynamically.
Set PGDATA to /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata and fsGroup: 70 so Postgres can use the PVC.
If pods CrashLoop from an earlier attempt, delete the StatefulSet and its PVCs, then re-apply.
Work only in your lab namespace (not default).
Read SPEC carefully, apply your YAML, then Submit.
problemStatement.solution:
# Solution — Stateful Orders Database

Create StatefulSet `orders-db` with 2 Postgres replicas, stable identity via `serviceName: orders-db`, and per-replica disks from `volumeClaimTemplates`.

Docs: [DevSetu Blog — StatefulSets](/play/devops-engineer/kubernetes/read/statefulsets) · [StatefulSets](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/statefulset/)

## Solution YAML

Save as `orders-db-sts-l20.yaml`:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: orders-db
spec:
  serviceName: orders-db
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: orders-db
      tier: data
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: orders-db
        tier: data
    spec:
      securityContext:
        fsGroup: 70
      containers:
        - name: postgres
          image: postgres:16-alpine
          ports:
            - containerPort: 5432
          env:
            - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
              value: quickbyte-lab
            - name: POSTGRES_DB
              value: orders
            - name: PGDATA
              value: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
          args: ["-c", "shared_buffers=16MB"]
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "20m"
              memory: "64Mi"
            limits:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "128Mi"
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data
  volumeClaimTemplates:
    - metadata:
        name: data
      spec:
        accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
        storageClassName: gp2
        resources:
          requests:
            storage: 500Mi
```

## Why `PGDATA` and `fsGroup`

- Mount the PVC at `/var/lib/postgresql/data`, but set **`PGDATA`** to a subdirectory so Postgres does not treat the volume root (e.g. `lost+found`) as the data dir.
- **`fsGroup: 70`** lets the alpine `postgres` user write the volume.

## Declarative

```bash
# If a previous attempt CrashLoop'd, delete STS + PVCs so disks re-init cleanly:
kubectl delete sts orders-db --ignore-not-found
kubectl delete pvc -l app=orders-db --ignore-not-found

kubectl apply -f orders-db-sts-l20.yaml
kubectl get sts orders-db
kubectl get pods -l app=orders-db -o wide
kubectl get pvc -l app=orders-db
```

Wait until **2/2** replicas are Ready, then **Submit**. Use a StatefulSet (not a Deployment).
